youtube.title: The 4 Alarms That Let You Stop Watching Your AI Agents
youtube.description:
Every guide to running AI agents ends with the same advice: keep a human in the loop. None of them say what that human is supposed to be looking at. Reading every output can't work, because agents don't fail loudly: a confused agent writes something fluent and plausible, which is exactly what working output looks like.

The answer is to stop checking whether the output is good and start checking whether it has the right shape. Four alarms, each a condition that cannot be true if your agent team is working, checked automatically on every run:
1. The run that produced nothing, including runs stuck waiting for approval.
2. The step that never says no: a filtering agent that passes everything through.
3. The missing field: required information checked in code, not requested in a prompt.
4. The bill: a per-run spending cap with an alert at half, and cost per useful output.

Then how to wire them up so they reach you, why you should break each one on purpose to test it, how to keep alarms from becoming noise, and the one five-minute habit that covers what alarms can't.
